facts.raw_span: a 2-month history of intermittent painless hematuria with passage of clots
denied dysuria, frequency, or other lower urinary tract symptoms
no family history of malignancy
vital signs and abdominal and pelvic exams were unremarkable
hemoglobin level of 8.6 g/dL
serum creatinine and other biochemical parameters were within normal limits
a 2.9 × 2.5 × 2.4 cm polypoidal mass arising from the posterolateral wall of the bladder dome
pre- and postvoid bladder volumes were 180 mL and 44 mL, respectively
an exophytic solid tumor measuring 1.5 × 2.0 cm on the anterior fundal wall, covered with slough
Histopathological analysis revealed an adenocarcinoma composed of mucinous and signet-ring cell components
a secondary adenocarcinoma or a rare variant of primary adenocarcinoma of the bladder was suspected
a deep transurethral resection of the bladder tumor was performed

concepts.why: The patient presented with a 2-month history of intermittent painless hematuria with passage of clots, and histopathological analysis revealed an adenocarcinoma composed of mucinous and signet-ring cell components.
The patient presented with a 2-month history of intermittent painless hematuria with passage of clots.
The patient had a hemoglobin level of 8.6 g/dL, requiring blood transfusion.
The patient had a 2.9 × 2.5 × 2.4 cm polypoidal mass arising from the posterolateral wall of the bladder dome.
The patient had a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
The patient had a history of hypertension.
The patient had a history of ischemic heart disease.
The patient had a suspected secondary adenocarcinoma or a rare variant of primary adenocarcinoma of the bladder.

rationales.F01: Painless hematuria is a common symptom of urinary bladder adenocarcinoma.
rationales.F03: No family history of malignancy reduces the likelihood of metastatic adenocarcinoma.
rationales.F05: Low hemoglobin level indicates anemia, which can be caused by hematuria.
rationales.F07: The presence of a polypoidal mass in the bladder is highly suggestive of a bladder tumor.
rationales.F09: The exophytic solid tumor on the anterior fundal wall is consistent with a bladder tumor.
rationales.F10: Histopathological analysis revealing adenocarcinoma is diagnostic of urinary bladder adenocarcinoma.
rationales.F11: The suspicion of a secondary adenocarcinoma or a rare variant of primary adenocarcinoma of the bladder is based on the histopathological findings.
